newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds were lifted from their day's lows by German inflation data but still closed down as higher yielding markets hogged the spotlight.
The yield discount to Germany, which reached 16 basis points in September, continued to narrow to four basis points, a level last seen in July, as guilder paper underperformed Bunds.
News that west German inflation data in October was better than expected buoyed the markets, but the guilder's recent fall against the market continued.
"All these (factors) point to less strength in the Netherlands (bond market)," said one fixed interest analyst.
Dealers and fund managers said the Dutch market remained quiet, with few real buyers or sellers, becalmed most recently by Italy's re-entry to the exchange rate mechanism.
This has increased interest in higher-yielding currencies such as the lira, at the expense of the guilder and the mark.
"Everyone is so bullish about (Economic and Monetary Union) going on in 1999. They're jumping on high-yielders," said a portfolio manager.
A trader said he was negative on Dutch bonds, expecting the 10-year yield, now 5.75 percent, to rise to six percent by year end. -- Garry West, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
